newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ESTONIAN BANKS TALK ON JOINT OPTIONS TRADE SYSTEM.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIAN BANKS TALK ON JOINT OPTIONS TRADE SYSTEM.

text.p: Three banks have started preliminary talks on the development of a standardised stock options trading system, Hansapank said on Wednesday.
"We have started preliminary talks to standardise stock option trading systems as a first step to trade in each others options," said Tonis Haavel, options trader with Hansapank.
"Talks with Hoiupank began in May and our lawyers have reached an agreement which gives us both similar systems," he told Reuters.
Hansapank has also started talks with Forekspank and Haavel expected that a standardised system would be in operation within a year.
"The long-term aim of the process is for banks to buy and sell each others options," Haavel added.
The main advantage of the joint system would be to allow banks to cover their risk when dealing with bigger orders by buying options from other banks.
"We will also get a better picture of volatility levels and develop some volatility trading as presently most trading is pure directional trading," he added.
Hansapank has been trading options using a book system since November 1996 with long-term options at three months and a maturity date on the third Friday of each month.
Trade in the instruments was around eight million kroons last week.
